subparts.derivation: bᵀx=5, so λ=5/9=5/9; multiply λ by b.

subparts.derivation: Multiply Bλ to get p=[5, 2, -1]. Difference r=x-p=[1, -2, 1]; squared error rᵀr=6.
subparts.checks: This is the Euclidean norm, not the squared norm. For any other Bη, ||x-Bη||²=||r||²+||B(λ-η)||² because Bᵀr=0; hence p is the closest point.

subparts.derivation: The coefficient map is λ=G⁻¹Bᵀx; composing with B gives P=BG⁻¹Bᵀ, G⁻¹=[[5/6, -1/2], [-1/2, 1/2]].
subparts.checks: P is a 3×3 symmetric matrix; rank 2 since columns of B are independent.

subparts.derivation: Bᵀr=Bᵀx-Gλ=0. Also P²=BG⁻¹(BᵀB)G⁻¹Bᵀ=BG⁻¹GG⁻¹Bᵀ=P. This algebra proves orthogonality and idempotence.
subparts.conclusion: Both b1ᵀr and b2ᵀr vanish; P²=P.
